comment: The current three-component classification understates the architectural capabilities illustrated by the Spanish example. Spain provides a relevant example of a shared identity layer through BDPP-SNS/CIP-SNS; federated clinical-document exchange through HCDSNS; interoperable electronic prescription and dispensation; common semantic/modelling services; and connection to European cross-border services. Reflecting these capabilities would make the case study substantially more useful to implementers because it demonstrates how several foundational and health-specific DPI components can coexist in a decentralised national health system.
